summary: This article explains why rare, heavy rain in a dry desert can turn a dry wadi into a dangerous flash flood within minutes, how people stay safe, and how floodwater also brings life to the land.
introduce: Write “Problem” and “Solution” on the board and give pairs thirty seconds to think of a problem people face in daily life and one way to fix it. Explain that as they read “Rain in the Desert: Flash Floods”, they will look for the main problem and how it is solved.

keyTerms.def: rain water that flows over the ground instead of soaking in
to take in or soak up a liquid
happening very quickly and without warning

challengeTerms.def: very dry because there is little rain
a layer of rock or sand underground that holds water
water that falls from the sky, such as rain, snow, or hail

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that rain in the desert does more good than harm? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain, step by step, how a storm can turn a dry wadi into a flash flood.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review runoff, absorb, and sudden, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use arid, aquifer, and precipitation in a short paragraph that suggests a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
